amendments.body: crates/tank_core/src/types/geometry.rs:19 still defines `TankGeometry::water_volume_l()` as gross filled volume, and crates/tank_core/src/types/geometry.rs:56 plus crates/tank_core/src/types/geometry.rs:65 build ratio helpers on that same gross basis, while crates/tank_core/src/types/state.rs:177 defines `TankState::water_volume_l()` as the new canonical net-water volume. Leaving both public APIs under the same `water_volume_l` name preserves two incompatible meanings of water volume and makes future concentration/normalization code easy to wire back to gross volume. Rename the geometry-side gross helpers or move the canonical name there so callers only have one public `water_volume_l` semantics.
amendments.rationale: This is a significant maintainability risk: the task is supposed to establish one canonical concentration/volume API, but the current public surface still exposes an easy path back to the pre-migration gross-vs-net mistake.

payload.summary: `git diff` at HEAD was empty, so I reviewed the task-related implementation state directly. I found one significant maintainability risk: the new net-volume helper API coexists with a public gross-volume `TankGeometry::water_volume_l()` API under the same name.
